name: Elon Musk
desc: Controls the empire through votes, not ownership
metric: Owns 42% of SpaceX but controls 82.4% of the votes
facts: His new SpaceX deal, the largest pay package in history, hands him the votes upfront | But the shares only vest if SpaceX hits $7.5 trillion and 1 million people live on Mars | Tesla stake of about $277B, now held in shares after he exercised his 2018 options on June 16, 2026 | SpaceX stake of about 5.2 billion Class B shares per its S-1/A | SpaceX listed on Nasdaq on June 12, 2026, lifting his net worth past $1 trillion
take: The gap is the whole story. He owns far less than he controls. In SpaceX he holds 42% of the money but 82.4% of the votes. Watch whether his voting control keeps climbing even as outside shareholders pour money in.

name: SpaceX
desc: Rockets, Starlink internet, and now AI
facts: Listed Jun 12 2026 on Nasdaq as SPCX at a $135 IPO price | Three segments: Space, Connectivity, AI | Absorbed xAI (Grok) and X in the Feb 2026 merger | Net loss of $4.94B in 2025, and a $4.28B loss in Q1 2026 | Total losses since 2002 top $41.3B
take: The cleanest version of the whole map. Public money in, near-total control kept. The number I watch is whether AI's losses ever force a change.

name: Tesla
desc: Electric cars, batteries, self-driving and robots
facts: ~1.64M vehicles delivered in 2025 | Q1 2026 auto gross margin was 19.2%, up from 16.3% a year earlier | Bought $2B of SpaceX equity in Q1 2026 | Raised 2026 capex guidance to over $25B, and ended Model S and X production in May 2026 | One share, one vote: no super-voting shares | Exercised 304 million 2018-package options on June 16, 2026, paying the strike with withheld shares and no open-market sale
take: Revenue actually fell in 2025. Cars are not the growth story anymore. The number I watch now is energy, not deliveries.

name: The Boring Company
desc: Digs tunnels for underground transit (the Loop)
facts: Runs the Las Vegas Loop, 4M+ riders across about 11 stations | Airport service to Harry Reid opened late 2025, about $12 a ride | Signed Dubai Loop deal, 6.4 km and 4 stations, tunneling late 2026 | Privately funded by casinos and developers, no taxpayer money | ~$908M raised, last priced round Series C in 2022 | Valuation has slipped to around $7B on secondary estimates
take: Still the quiet one, but the Dubai deal and the airport line show it is finally moving, even as the valuation lags.

name: Neuralink
desc: Brain implants that let people control devices by thought
facts: N1 implant in more than 20 patients by early 2026 | Raised about $1.85B total; Series E at $9B in June 2025 | Blindsight vision implant has FDA breakthrough status, first humans planned 2026 | Plans high-volume production and near-automated surgery in 2026 | Still pre-revenue, first revenue not projected until 2031
take: The highest-risk, longest-horizon company: real medical progress, no revenue. Locked away from public investors for now. Watch for any pre-IPO chatter.

name: Space
desc: Launch services and spacecraft, the rocket business
facts: Active vehicles: Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Dragon | The loss is driven by Starship R&D | Starship still in test flights
take: The original business now loses money on purpose. Every spare dollar feeds Starship. The question is when Starship finally carries paying payloads.

name: Connectivity
desc: Starlink internet, plus Starshield for governments
facts: Almost all of this revenue is Starlink | Starshield is the government and defense layer, not broken out separately | About 63% EBITDA margin in 2025 | The cash engine that funds Starship and the AI buildout
take: This is the engine. Starlink is the only part throwing off real cash, and it bankrolls all of SpaceX. Remember this one number.

name: AI
desc: Grok AI and the X social network
facts: Formed by folding xAI (Grok) and X into SpaceX in Feb 2026 | Runs the Colossus data centers in Memphis; Colossus 2 came online in Jan 2026 with 555,000 Nvidia GPUs and 2 gigawatts of power | Leases compute to Anthropic at $1.25B a month and Google at about $920M a month, roughly $26B a year combined | Both compute deals can be cancelled on 90 days notice | May 2026: cleared by the Pentagon for its most sensitive data, IL6 and IL7
take: Real revenue, bigger losses. The thing is this segment could justify the whole valuation or sink it. Watch the compute deals.

name: Falcon 9
desc: The reusable rocket that funds the space business
facts: 123 of the 165 launches were SpaceX's own Starlink missions | Reusability is the edge, with some boosters past 30 flights | List price is about $74 million per launch | 2025 was the peak; flights ease off as SpaceX shifts to Starship
take: The quiet cash-and-reputation engine. 165 launches in a year, mostly its own Starlink. This is what funds the moonshots.

name: Starship
desc: The giant next-generation rocket aimed at Mars
metric: Flight 12 flew May 22, 2026; Flight 13, the first orbital attempt, is Q3 2026 at the earliest
facts: Version 3 carries 100 tons to orbit, versus about 23 for Falcon 9 | Flight 12 lost one engine but held its trajectory | Flight 13 is the first orbital attempt, pending an FAA review | Built to launch the new Starlink V3 satellites in the second half of 2026
take: The biggest bet inside SpaceX. The thing is everything waits on it: Mars, Starlink V3, the next decade. Watch Flight 13 for the first orbit.

name: Starlink
desc: Consumer and business satellite internet
metric: 10.3M subscribers as of Q1 2026, up 105% YoY
facts: Revenue per user fell from $99 a month in 2023 to $66 in Q1 2026 | Runs about 9,600 satellites, roughly 65% of all active satellites | Beams direct to phones in about 30 countries | Tested a $39 a month floor in March 2026, then raised prices $5 to $10 in May 2026 | Churn rate is still not disclosed
take: Subscribers keep climbing while revenue per user keeps falling. The thing is I do not know which one wins. Watch which sets the trajectory.

name: Starshield
desc: A secure satellite network for defense and government
facts: The national-security version of Starlink | Won a $2.29B Starshield contract in 2026
take: The quiet, high-margin government layer most retail investors never hear about. Just landed a $2.29B defense contract.

name: Grok
desc: The xAI chatbot, built to rival ChatGPT
metric: Now runs Starlink's support line, resolving 70% of calls before a human
facts: About 117 million people use Grok features | Handles Starlink customer support, with 1 in 5 callers buying on the call | SpaceX exercised its option to buy the coding tool Cursor for $60 billion in SpaceX stock on June 16, 2026, set to close in Q3 2026, partly for its data to retrain Grok | Grok 5 is training on the Colossus 2 cluster
take: The product SpaceX is spending heavily to rebuild. The thing is the data is the moat. Watch whether Cursor closes the gap.

name: X
desc: The social network formerly called Twitter
facts: About 350 million posts a day | Around 550 million monthly users across X and Grok | Bought by Elon in 2022, folded into the AI segment in 2026
take: Bought for $44B, folded into the AI bet. The thing is its real worth now is the data it feeds Grok.

name: Automotive
desc: Designing, building and selling electric vehicles
facts: ~1.64M vehicles delivered in 2025 | Q1 2026 deliveries 358k, missed estimates, built ~50k excess inventory | Q2 2026 deliveries hit a record 480,126, up 25% YoY and beating estimates by 74,000 cars, yet the stock fell 7.49% the same day | 2025 auto revenue fell about 10% despite flat volume | Still Tesla's largest revenue source
take: This is still the cash engine. But nobody is buying Tesla stock for car sales anymore.

name: Energy
desc: Batteries for homes and the grid (Powerwall, Megapack)
facts: Record 46.7 GWh of storage deployed in 2025, up 49% | Powerwall for homes, Megapack for grids | Megapack 3 and Megablock launched; Houston targets 50 GWh | Quarterly revenue is lumpy by project timing
take: Storage up 49% in a year while cars stalled. The thing is this might be the real growth engine now, not autonomy.

name: Full Self-Driving
desc: Tesla's self-driving software, the bet on autonomy
metric: Sold per car or as a monthly subscription
facts: Sold as Full Self-Driving (Supervised), the branch that also powers Robotaxi | 10 billion cumulative FSD miles by May 2026, near 20 million a day | China: a limited version switched on May 21 2026, full approval still pending and targeted for Q3 2026 | Europe: Netherlands, Lithuania, Estonia and Denmark all rest on one Dutch approval (Apr 10 2026) that is still temporary and needs a full EU vote to become permanent | Under a US safety investigation covering about 3.2 million vehicles | v15 is the release that gates wide consumer rollout and opt-in | Hardware 3 cars (2019 to 2023) cannot run unsupervised FSD
take: This is where the valuation quietly moved. The cars fund it, the software is the bet, and the approvals in China and Europe are the trigger now.

name: Optimus
desc: Tesla's humanoid robot
metric: Pilot production began Jan 2026, scaling targeted late 2026
facts: Gen 3 pilot production began at Fremont, Jan 2026 | Still only learning and data collection, no productive work yet | Fremont line converting from Model S and X, targets 1M a year | 2026 production target 50,000 to 100,000 units | Chinese makers shipped 10,000+ humanoids in 2025, one at $5,900 | Analyst values range from near zero to about $93B
take: Real ambition, no revenue yet. Elon admits none do useful work. Pure optionality until pilot lines turn into real production numbers.

name: Model 3 & Y
desc: The two mass-market cars that carry Tesla's volume
facts: Among the best-selling EVs in the world | Tesla launched a new cheaper trim, the Model Y Standard, in 2026 | Volume has flattened
take: These two are the whole volume story. And the volume has flat-lined. That is the stalled-growth case in two cars.

name: Other Vehicles
desc: The rest of the lineup beyond the mass-market cars
metric: Model S, X, Cybertruck and Semi
facts: Cybertruck sales fell about 48% in 2025, to about 20,000 | Nearly 20% of Q4 Cybertrucks went to Musk's own firms | Tesla Semi began mass production in Nevada, March 2026 | Semi factory targets 50,000 trucks a year | Model S and X production ended May 2026 | Lower volume, higher price or niche
take: Cybertruck fell about 48%, and a fifth of them went to Musk's own companies. Semi is the quiet new bet here.

name: FSD Subscription
desc: Monthly subscription revenue from self-driving
facts: Monthly subscription for FSD (Supervised) | High-margin recurring revenue | FSD take rate near 14% of the fleet | Outright FSD purchase mostly removed Feb 2026, subscription-first
take: Tesla used to hide this. Now it is disclosed, growing, high-margin. Real recurring revenue, finally, at about 14% of the fleet.

name: Robotaxi
desc: The autonomous ride-hailing service
facts: Live in 5 cities now: Austin, Bay Area, Dallas, Houston and Miami (Miami launched Jul 3 2026) | Only about 20 cars are actually carrying paying riders, vs Waymo's 3,000 and Elon's own 1,000-car target | Miami launched with no safety monitor from day one, the first city outside Texas to do that | Austin's paying fleet fell from 19 cars to 14 by mid-Jun 2026 | Remote operators move stuck cars; 2 of 17 NHTSA incidents were theirs | Tesla still won't publish the per-mile intervention rate, the key number
take: Everyone counts cars against Waymo's 3,000. The thing is that may be the wrong race. The number that decides it, Tesla still won't publish.

name: TeraFab
desc: Chip fabs planned for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI
facts: Two sites: a research fab on Tesla's Austin campus and a production fab planned for Grimes County, Texas | First floated at Tesla's November 2025 shareholder meeting, announced March 2026 | Grimes County's signed agreement requires only $5B by 2030, a fraction of the public pledge | County approved a 100% property tax abatement for 2027 to 2036 on a 4 to 1 vote | Targets 1,800 jobs by 2035 | Intel joined the project and would supply its 14A process | SpaceX's S-1 calls the arrangement a general framework with no binding terms
take: Tesla announced this and is paying to set it up, while the S-1 says SpaceX keeps the production fab. The thing I watch is whether a binding, signed deal ever replaces the general framework.
